Surah 51: Adh-Dhariyat

Meccan in its entirety, by consensus.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By the scatterers, scattering﴾ means the winds. It is said: the wind scattered (dharat) the dust, scatters it (tadhruwuhu) with a scattering (dharwan), when it disperses it. Al-Zajjaj said: it is said dharat, so it is dhariyah (scattering), and adharat, so it is mudhiyah (scattering), with one meaning.

﴿By the scatterers﴾ is in the genitive by way of oath. The meaning: I swear by the scatterers and these things. The response is ﴿What you are promised is surely true﴾. Some said: the meaning is "by the Lord of the scatterers, and the Lord of the runners."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿By the bearers of a burden﴾ means the clouds which carry their burden of water.

﴿By the runners, easily﴾ means the ships which run smoothly in [the water], a gentle running.

﴿By the distributors of a command﴾ means the angels who distribute affairs according to what God has commanded them. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: the distributors are four: Jibril, who is the bearer of revelation and of severity; Mika'il, who is the bearer of provision and mercy; Israfil, who is the bearer of the Trumpet and the Tablet; and 'Izra'il, who is the taker of souls. He swore by these things only because of the indications in them of His craftsmanship and power.

Then he mentioned what was sworn to, saying: ﴿What you are promised﴾, i.e., of reward and punishment on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿is surely true﴾, i.e., real.

﴿And indeed the Judgment﴾ has two interpretations.

One: the reckoning. The second: the recompense ﴿is surely to occur﴾, i.e., will certainly happen.

Then he mentioned another oath, saying: ﴿By the sky having paths﴾. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Razin read "al-hibik" with kasra on the ha and the ba together. 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, al-Sha'bi, Abu al-'Aliyah, and Abu Haywah read "al-hibk" with kasra on the ha and sukun on the ba. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Raja', and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "al-hubk" with damma on the ha and sukun on the ba. Ibn Mas'ud and 'Ikrimah read "al-habak" with fatha on the ha and the ba together.

(p-٢٩) Abu al-Darda', Abu al-Jawza', Abu al-Mutawakkil, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, and 'Asim al-Jahdari read ["al-habik"] with fatha on the ha and kasra on the ba.

Then regarding the meaning of ﴿al-hubuk﴾ there are four sayings. One: possessing good creation; this was narrated by Ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, and Qatadah said likewise. The second: solid construction, said by Mujahid. The third: possessing adornment, said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr. al-Hasan said: its hubuk are its stars. The fourth: possessing paths, said by al-Dahhak and the linguists. al-Farra' said: hubuk is the cracking/rippling of anything like sand when still wind passes over it, and of standing water when wind passes over it, and of curly hair, its rippling is hubuk; the singular of hubuk is hibak and habikah. al-Zajjaj said: the people of language say: hubuk are fine paths, and the mahbuk in language is that whose work has been perfected, and everything you see of paths in water and in sand when the wind touches it is hubuk. It was narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr that he said: this is the seventh heaven.

Then he mentioned the response to the second oath, saying: ﴿Indeed you﴾, meaning the people of Makkah, ﴿are in a contradictory saying﴾ concerning the matter of Muhammad ﷺ: some of you say he is a poet, and some of you say he is a madman. And regarding the Qur'an, [some of you] say it is magic, and some of you say it is soothsaying and rajaz, and so on.

﴿Turned away from it is whoever is turned away﴾, i.e., whoever is diverted from belief in it [is deprived of it]. [The pronoun in "'anhu" refers to the Qur'an. It was also said: whoever is turned away from this saying, i.e., because of it and its cause, from belief.] Qatadah read "man afak" with fatha on the alif and the fa. 'Amr ibn Dinar read "man afik" with fatha on the alif and kasra on the fa.

﴿Killed are the conjecturers﴾. al-Farra' said: meaning [cursed] are the liars who said that the Prophet ﷺ is a magician, a liar, and a poet, conjecturing about what they have no knowledge of. In a narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas: they were the soothsayers. Ibn al-Anbari said: "killing," when it is reported of God, means cursing, because whoever God curses is like one who is killed and destroyed.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Who are in heedlessness﴾, i.e., in blindness and ignorance regarding the matter of the Hereafter, ﴿heedless﴾, i.e., unmindful. Sahw is unawareness of a thing and the heart's departure from it.

﴿They ask: when is the Day of Judgment?﴾, i.e., they say: O Muhammad, when is the Day of Recompense? In denial and mockery.

Then He informed about that day, saying: the Day when ﴿they will be over the Fire﴾. al-Zajjaj said: "the day" is in the accusative, meaning: the recompense occurs on the day when they are over the Fire, ﴿being tried﴾, i.e., burned and punished. From this, black stones that appear as if burned by fire are called fatin.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Taste your trial﴾. The meaning: it is said to them: taste your trial. Regarding it there are two sayings.

One: your denial, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: your burning, said by Mujahid. Abu 'Ubaydah said: here the speech is complete, then it is resumed, and He said: ﴿This is what you were seeking to hasten﴾. The commentators said: meaning what you used to seek to hasten in the world, mockingly. Then He mentioned what God promised the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿Indeed the righteous will be in gardens and springs﴾, and the explanation of this has already passed [al-Baqarah 25; al-Hijr 45].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Taking﴾. al-Zajjaj said: it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state, so the meaning: (p-٣١) in gardens and springs, in the state of taking ﴿what their Lord has given them﴾. The commentators said: i.e., the honor God has bestowed on them. ﴿Indeed they were before that doers of good﴾ in their deeds. There is another interpretation of the verse: ﴿taking what their Lord has given them﴾, i.e., acting upon what He commanded them of obligations, ﴿indeed they were before﴾ the obligations were imposed upon them, ﴿doers of good﴾, i.e., obedient. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of Muslim al-Bateen.

Then he mentioned their goodness, saying: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night﴾. al-Huju': sleeping at night, not during the day.

Regarding "ma" there are two sayings. One: it is negation. Then regarding the meaning there are two sayings. One: they used to stay awake a little of the night. Anas ibn Malik and Abu al-'Aliyah said: it is what is between Maghrib and 'Isha'.

The second: they used not to sleep a little of the night. A group chose to stop at His saying ﴿little﴾, meaning: they were a little of the people; then he began: ﴿of the night, they sleep not﴾, meaning the complete negation of sleep from them. This is the view of al-Dahhak and Muqatil. (p-٣٢) The second saying: "ma" means "alladhi," so the meaning: they used to sleep little of the night, which they slept. This is the view of al-Hasan, al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, and al-Zuhri. On this view "ma" may be superfluous.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And in the pre-dawn hours they seek forgiveness﴾, which we have explained in [Ali 'Imran 17].

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right﴾, i.e., a share, and regarding it there are two sayings.

One: that it is what they give to relatives, or host a guest with, or carry a burden with, or help a deprived person with, and it is not the zakat; said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: that it is zakat; said by Qatadah and Ibn Sirin.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the beggar﴾, who is the seeker.

Regarding "al-mahrum" (the deprived) there are eight sayings.

One: that he is the one who has no share in the spoils of the Muslims, the destitute; said by Ibn 'Abbas. Ibrahim said: he is the one who has no share in the booty.

The second: that he is the one for whom nothing grows; said by Mujahid, and likewise 'Ata' said: he is the one deprived in provision and trade.

The third: that he is the poor Muslim; said by Muhammad ibn 'Ali.

The fourth: that he is the modest one who does not ask for anything; said by Qatadah and al-Zuhri.

The fifth: that he is the one who comes after the spoils and has no share in them; said by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah.

(p-٣٣) The sixth: that he is the one whose fruit or crop or herd's offspring has been struck; said by Ibn Zayd.

The seventh: that he is the slave; related by al-Mawardi.

The eighth: that he is the dog; narrated from 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. al-Sha'bi used to say: I am unable to know what the mahrum is. The most apparent of the sayings is the saying of Qatadah and al-Zuhri, because He paired him with the beggar, and the modest one does not ask, and people hardly give to one who does not ask; then he guards himself through modesty from the appearance of the trace of need upon him, so he is deprived by his own self when he does not ask, and by people when they do not give him, and only the alert person perceives him. The commentators have mentioned that this verse is abrogated by the verse of zakat, but this is not sound.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And on the earth are signs﴾, such as mountains, rivers, trees, fruits, and other things, ﴿for those who are certain﴾ of God, the Mighty and Majestic, those who know Him through His craftsmanship.

﴿And in yourselves﴾ are signs, as you were drops, then bones, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, and other states of change; then the variation of forms, colors, and natures; the straightening of the organs, hearing, sight, and reason; and the facilitation of the path of excrement, and other wonders deposited in the son of Adam. The statement was complete at His saying ﴿And in yourselves﴾, then He said: ﴿Will you not see?﴾ Muqatil said: Will you not see how He created you so that you might know His power over resurrection?

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And in the sky is your provision﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Humayd, (p-٣٤) and Abu Husayn al-Asadi read "arzaquكم" with a silent ra' and an alif between the za' and the qaf. Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak, and Abu Nuhayk read "raziquكم" with fatha on the ra' and kasra on the za' with an alif between them. Ibn Muhaysin is also reported with these two readings. Regarding it there are two sayings.

One: that it is rain; narrated by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and by Layth from Mujahid, and it is the saying of the majority.

The second: that it is Paradise; narrated by Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid.

Regarding His saying ﴿and what you are promised﴾ there are two sayings.

One: that it is good and evil, both of which come from the sky; said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid.

The second: that it is Paradise; narrated by Layth from Mujahid. Abu 'Ubaydah said: in this verse there is an implied meaning: the sense is "with the one who is in the sky is your provision, and with Him is what you are promised," and the Arabs omit (words). Nabighah [Dhubyan] said:

"As if you were one of the camels of Banu Uqaysh, rattled behind its legs by a water-skin."

He meant: as if you were a camel from the camels of Banu Uqaysh.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed it is truth﴾. al-Zajjaj said: meaning what He mentioned of the matter of the signs, the provision, what you are promised, and the matter of the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿Like what you speak﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr from 'Asim read "mithlu" with damma on the lam. The rest read it with fatha on the lam. al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads "mithlu" with damma, it is an attribute of the truth, meaning: it is truth like your speech; and whoever reads it with fatha, then it is in two ways. (p-٣٥) One: that it is in the place of nominative, except that when it was annexed to "anna" it took fatha. The second: that it is accusative as emphasis, meaning: it is truth, a truth like your speech; and this statement is like saying: it is true as you speak.

The second: that it is zakat; said by Qatadah and Ibn Sirin.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the beggar﴾, who is the seeker.

One: that he is the one who has no share in the spoils of the Muslims, the destitute; said by Ibn 'Abbas. Ibrahim said: he is the one who has no share in the booty.

The second: that he is the one for whom nothing grows; said by Mujahid, and likewise 'Ata' said: he is the one deprived in provision and trade.

The fourth: that he is the modest one who does not ask for anything; said by Qatadah and al-Zuhri.

Then he mentioned their goodness, saying: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night﴾. al-Huju': sleeping at night, not during the day.

The second: they used not to sleep a little of the night. One: that it is what they give to relatives, or host a guest with, or carry a burden with, or help a deprived person with, and it is not the zakat; said by Ibn 'Abbas.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the beggar﴾, who is the seeker.

One: that he is the one who has no share in the spoils of the Muslims, the destitute; said by Ibn 'Abbas. Ibrahim said: he is the one who has no share in the booty.

The second: that he is the one for whom nothing grows; said by Mujahid, and likewise 'Ata' said: he is the one deprived in provision and trade.

The third: that he is the poor Muslim; said by Muhammad ibn 'Ali.

The fourth: that he is the modest one who does not ask for anything; said by Qatadah and al-Zuhri.

The fifth: that he is the one who comes after the spoils and has no share in them; said by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah.

Ibn al-Anbari said: "killing," when it is reported of God, means cursing, because whoever God curses is like one who is killed and destroyed.

From this, black stones that appear as if burned by fire are called fatin.

One: your denial, said by Ibn 'Abbas. The second: your burning, said by Mujahid. Abu 'Ubaydah said: here the speech is complete, then it is resumed, and He said: ﴿This is what you were seeking to hasten﴾. The commentators said: meaning what you used to seek to hasten in the world, mockingly. The second: that it is zakat; said by Qatadah and Ibn Sirin.

One: that he is the one who has no share in the spoils of the Muslims, the destitute; said by Ibn 'Abbas. Ibrahim said: he is the one who has no share in the booty.

The second: that he is the one for whom nothing grows; said by Mujahid, and likewise 'Ata' said: he is the one deprived in provision and trade.

The third: that he is the poor Muslim; said by Muhammad ibn 'Ali.

The commentators have mentioned that this verse is abrogated by the verse of zakat, but this is not sound.

﴿And in yourselves﴾ are signs, as you were drops, then bones, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, and other states of change; then the variation of forms, colors, and natures; the straightening of the organs, hearing, sight, and reason; and the facilitation of the path of excrement, and other wonders deposited in the son of Adam. The statement was complete at His saying ﴿And in yourselves﴾, then He said: ﴿Will you not see?﴾ Muqatil said: Will you not see how He created you so that you might know His power over resurrection?

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And in the sky is your provision﴾. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Humayd, (p-٣٤) and Abu Husayn al-Asadi read "arzaquكم" with a silent ra' and an alif between the za' and the qaf. Regarding it there are two sayings.

One: that it is rain; narrated by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and by Layth from Mujahid, and it is the saying of the majority.

The second: that it is Paradise; narrated by Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid.

Regarding His saying ﴿and what you are promised﴾ there are two sayings.

One: that it is good and evil, both of which come from the sky; said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid.

The second: that it is Paradise; narrated by Layth from Mujahid. Abu 'Ubaydah said: in this verse there is an implied meaning: the sense is "with the one who is in the sky is your provision, and with Him is what you are promised," and the Arabs omit (words). Nabighah [Dhubyan] said:

He meant: as if you were a camel from the camels of Banu Uqaysh.

The second: that it is accusative as emphasis, meaning: it is truth, a truth like your speech; and this statement is like saying: it is true as you speak.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 51, verse 24–37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has there reached you the story of the honored guests of Abraham?﴾ "Hal" (has) here means "qad" (indeed) according to the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil, so the meaning is: "Indeed it has reached you, so listen, and we will relate it to you." His guests are those who came with the glad tidings. We have mentioned their number in [Hud: 70], and we mentioned there the meaning of "guest" (dayf).

Regarding the meaning of "the honored" (al-mukramin) there are four opinions:

The first: because he honored them with the calf. This was said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid also said it.

The second: because he and his wife served them with their own selves. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: because they are honored with God. This was said by 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya.

The fourth: because they are guests, and guests are honored. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Warraq.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Peace!"﴾ We have mentioned it in [Hud: 70].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿"A people unknown."﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: it is in the nominative on the meaning: "You are a people unknown."

For the exegetes there are four opinions regarding the cause of their being unknown to him.

The first: because he did not know them. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: because they greeted him with peace, and he denied their greeting in that time and in that land. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The third: because they entered [upon him] without seeking permission.

The fourth: because he saw in them the form of humans and the form of angels.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he turned quietly to his family﴾ Ibn Qutaybah said: that is, he turned to them secretly, and "al-riwagh" does not mean that you conceal your going and coming.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then he brought a fatted calf﴾ and it was roasted, ﴿and placed it before them.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that he placed it before them so that they would eat from it, but they did not eat, so he said: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ in disapproval, meaning: your refusing to eat is something I disapprove of.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he felt a fear of them﴾ We have explained it in [Hud: 70], and we mentioned the meaning of "a knowing boy" in [al-Hijr: 54].

﴿Then his wife came forward﴾ and she was Sarah. Al-Farra' and Ibn Qutaybah said: she did not come from one place to another; rather it is like your saying: "He began to abuse me" and "He began to shout and speak," meaning he undertook that. "Al-sarrah" is the cry, and Abu 'Ubaydah said: "al-sarrah" is intensity of voice.

Regarding what she said in her outcry there are two opinions.

The first: that she struck her face in lament, said by Qatadah.

The second: that she said: "Woe is me!" mentioned by al-Farra'.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and she struck her face﴾ There are two opinions concerning it.

The first: she slapped her face. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: she struck her forehead in amazement. This was said by Mujahid. The meaning of "sakk" is striking one thing against a broad thing.

﴿And said an old woman﴾ Al-Farra' said: this is in the nominative by an implied "Does an old woman bear?" Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: I am an old, barren woman, so how shall I bear? We have mentioned the meaning of "barren" (aqim) in [Hud: 72].

﴿They said: "Thus has your Lord said,"﴾ that you will bear a boy; the meaning is: we only inform you about God, mighty and majestic, who is All-Wise, All-Knowing, able to make the barren fertile. Then Abraham knew [at that point] that they were angels.

﴿He said: "What is your business, O messengers?"﴾ It is explained in [al-Hijr: 57].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿stones of clay﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: it is baked brick.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿marked by your Lord﴾ We have explained it in [Hud: 83]. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿for the transgressors﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: for the polytheists.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We brought out whoever was there﴾ that is, from the towns of Lot, (of the believers). This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So travel with your family...﴾ the verse [Hud: 82].

﴿But We found not therein any but one house of the Muslims﴾ and it was Lot and his two daughters. God, mighty and majestic, described them with faith and Islam, because every believer is a Muslim.

﴿And We left therein a sign﴾ that is, a sign for those who fear the punishment of God, showing them that God destroyed them. We have explained this in [al-'Ankabut: 35] and clarified what is meant by it.

The first: because he honored them with the calf. This was said by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid also said it.

The second: because he and his wife served them with their own selves. This was said by al-Suddi.

The third: because they are honored with God. This was said by 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya.

The fourth: because they are guests, and guests are honored. This was said by Abu Bakr al-Warraq.

For the exegetes there are four opinions regarding the cause of their being unknown to him.

The first: because he did not know them. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: because they greeted him with peace, and he denied their greeting in that time and in that land. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The third: because they entered [upon him] without seeking permission.

The fourth: because he saw in them the form of humans and the form of angels.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 51, verse 38–51:

The Most High said: ﴿And in ʿĀd [too there is a sign], when We sent upon them the barren wind (al-rīḥ al-ʿaqīm)﴾. That is, in their destruction there is also a sign. It is the wind in which there is no good and no blessing; it does not fertilize trees nor bring rain, and it is only for destruction. Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: it is the south wind (al-Janūb).

﴿That leaves nothing it comes upon without making it like that which is crumbled (kal-ramīm)﴾. That is, [it destroys] of their persons and their wealth. ﴿Like that which is crumbled﴾: like a perished, decayed thing. Al-Farrāʾ said: al-ramīm is the vegetation of the earth when it dries up and is trampled. Al-Zajjāj said: al-ramīm is dry, brittle leaves, crushed like al-hashīm (dry stubble).

﴿And in Thamūd [too there is a sign], when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a while (ḥattā ḥīn)"﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves in this world until the end of your appointed terms," as a threat to them.

The second: after they hamstrung the she-camel, Ṣāliḥ said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for three days." So the ḥīn was the time of the end of their terms. ﴿But they defied the command of their Lord﴾. Muqātil said: they disobeyed His command. ﴿So the thunderbolt (al-ṣāʿiqah) seized them﴾, meaning the punishment, which was death, from the cry of Jibrīl.

Al-Kisāʾī alone read: "al-ṣaʿqah" [with a sukūn on the ʿayn and without an alif]; it is the sound that comes from the thunderbolt.

The Most High said: ﴿while they were looking on (wa-hum yanẓurūn)﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: they were seeing it with their own eyes. The second: they were awaiting the punishment, and a cry came to them on the day of Saturday.

The Most High said: ﴿so they were not able to rise up (fa-mā istaṭāʿū min qiyām)﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions.

The first: they were not able to rise from that fall.

The second: they had no strength to withstand the punishment of Allah. ﴿And they were not able to defend themselves (wa-mā kānū muntaṣirīn)﴾, that is, they could not protect themselves from the punishment.

The Most High said: ﴿And the people of Nūh before [them] (wa-qawma Nūḥin min qablu)﴾. Abū ʿAmr, except ʿAbd al-Wārith, and Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read it with a kasrah on the mīm; ʿAbd al-Wārith related it with a ḍammah on the mīm, and the rest read it with a fatḥah. Al-Zajjāj said: whoever reads al-qawm with a kasrah, the meaning is: and in the people of Nūḥ there is a sign. Whoever reads it with a fatḥah, it is coordinated with the meaning of His words ﴿so the thunderbolt seized them﴾, for its meaning is: We destroyed them; so the meaning is: and We destroyed the people of Nūḥ. The third: We are capable (la-qādirūn); this is said by Ibn Qutaybah. The fourth: We are expanding the space between the heaven and the earth; this is said by al-Zajjāj. The fifth: We are One of vast capacity who is not constrained in what He wills; related by al-Māwardī.

The Most High said: ﴿And the earth — We spread it out, and how excellent are We as spreaders (fa-niʿma al-māhidūn)﴾. Al-Zajjāj said: this is coordinated with what precedes it, governed by an implied verb indicated by His words ﴿We spread it out﴾; so the meaning is: We spread out the earth, We spread it out, ﴿and how excellent are the spreaders﴾, that is, how excellent are We as spreaders. The Most High said: ﴿And of every thing We created pairs (zawjayn)﴾, that is, two kinds and two types, such as male and female, land and sea, night and day, the sweet and the bitter, light and darkness, and similar things, ﴿so that you may remember﴾, and thus you may know that the Creator of the pairs is One.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So let them not ask Me to hasten﴾, that is, the punishment, if they are delayed until the Day of Resurrection, which is ﴿their day that they are promised﴾. It is said: it is the Day of Badr.
